factions.name: Belgium
additionalRules: Forward Artillery Doctrine - The Artillery Forward Observer unit may call an artillery barrage twice instead of once per game. Resolve the first barrage as normal. Then, after the first barrage has been resolved, the observer may call a second (when issued a Fire order); Bolt Action, April 2025 Get-You-By Belgium PDF

Highly Motivated Reserves - Every Inexperienced unit that has one or more pin markers can make a test to lose one pin marker if there are any enemy units within 12in immediately before an order is given to it. For example, a unit of infantry has two pin markers and there is an enemy unit within 12in - when the infantry are allocated an order they can test to lose one pin marker immediately before the order test is taken. Roll a die: on a roll of 4, 5 or 6 the test is passed and the unit loses one pin marker; on a 1, 2 or 3 the test is failed and the unit retains the pin markers it has. Once this has been done, continue to test to see if the unit obeys its order in the usual way, even if they have lost their last pin marker (in which case the order test is taken without negative modifiers from pin markers); Bolt Action, April 2025 Get-You-By Belgium PDF

factions.name: Bulgaria
additionalRules: Axis Support - A Bulgarian force may include a single unit from either the German or Italian army lists (though no German or Italian army special rules apply, except for Hitler's Buzz Saw). This unit must be included as part of a platoon, taking the slot of hte equivalent unit type (e.g. a sniper team for a sniper team, a tank for a tank), and may not be one of that platoon's mandatory units. In addition, this unit may not be a Veteran unit, nor a vehicle with a Damage Value of 10 or higher; Bolt Action, April 2025 Get-You-By Bulgaria PDF
Roving Patrols - Enemies cannot make Outflanking Maneuvers and cannot use the Infiltrators special rule for deployment; Bolt Action, February 2026 Get-You-By Bulgaria PDF

factions.name: Finland
additionalRules: Trained Huntsmen - As long as any Finnish infantry unit has an Ambush order die next to it, it can re-roll morale checks. Also, when the unit opens fire from Ambush, all models in the unit that are armed with a rifle, including snipers, gain an additional +1 to-hit bonus; Bolt Action, April 2025 Get-You-By Finland PDF

Sisu - When a Finnish infantry or artillery unit is reduced to 50 per cent or less of its starting strength, the remaining models in that unit are automatically upgraded to higher quality - Inexperienced troops become Regular and Regulars become Veterans, while Veteran units increase their base Morale to 11. For example, when a unit of 9 Regular Finnish infantry is reduced to 4 men or below, the men immediately upgrade to Veterans before any more dice are rolled (including any Morale check they must take for the casualties just suffered); Bolt Action, April 2025 Get-You-By Finland PDF

Motti - When attempting an outflanking maneuver as described on p.172 of the Bolt Action rulebook, Finnish infantry units ignore the -1 modifier to the Order test for coming on to the table; Bolt Action, April 2025 Get-You-By Finland PDF
Skis - All infantry units may be equipped with skis for free. Ski troops ignore movement penalties for snow and other winter conditions; Bolt Action, April 2025 Get-You-By Finland PDF

factions.name: Italy
additionalRules: Defensive Strategy - The player can re-roll the die on the Artillery Barrage and Smoke Barrage table. During the first turn of the game, the enemy cannot order their units on the table to Run as they cautiously probe the terrain in front of the Italian line for minefields and make their way across the barbed wire. Units deployed as part of a first wave can be ordered to Run as normal to enter the table. Any Italian unit that is set up on the table before Turn 1 may start the game in Ambush. If you decide to do so, set one of your order dice in place next to them, as if you had ordered them to Ambush, before drawing the first order die on Turn 1; Bolt Action, April 2025 Get-You-By Italy PDF

factions.name: Japan
additionalRules: Death Before Dishonor - All Imperial Japanese infantry and artillery units have the Fanatics special rule. In addition, they automatically pass morale checks for being assaulted by enemy tanks (note that artillery pieces are still destroyed as normal).

Banzai! - A Japanese Officer may be given a special 'Banzai!' order. THis counts as a 'You Men Snap to Action' with the following exceptions: If the order is given successfully, assign the officer a Run order die. THen ALL infantry units within 6in that haven't already received an order that turn are issued a Run order. NOte that this includes infantry units with the Fixed special rule, like many weapon teams. All affected units, including the initiating officer, must then attempt to engage the closest visible enemy unit in close quarters. Note that, other than for the initiating officer, no order test is required for any units affected by a 'Banzai!' order. This means that affected units execute their Run orders automatically, without any dice rolled, and as such retain any pin markers they have.

Lack of Radios - When you give the Command Vehicle special rule to a vehicle that does not have it in its entry for the purposes of choosing a command vehicle for an Armoured Platoon, you can give it the rule for free instead of paying the normal +10pts. If you do so, the vehicle reduces its Command Vehicle rule from 12in to 6in. This represents communication by means of flags or hand signals.

factions.name: Soviet Union
additionalRules: The Great Patriotic War - Whenever a unit of infantry or artillery models fails a morale check and would otherwise be destroyed as a consequence, take the test again and apply this second result. THis re-roll applies to all infantry and artillery units and not to vehicles.

For the Motherland! - Every Inexperienced unit that has one or more pin markers can make a test to lose one pin marker if there are any enemy within 12in immediately before an order is given to it. Roll a die: on a roll of 4, 5 or 6 the test is passed and the unit loses one pin marker; on a 1, 2 or 3 the test is failed and the unit retains the pin markers it has. Once this has been done, continue to test to see if the unit obeys its order in the usual way, even if they have lost their last pin marker.

Not One Step Back! - Soviet armies may include a single commissar for each Rifle Platoon. Commissars are political officers and do not confer a morale bonus to nearby troops. When a friendly infantry unit fails an order test within 6in of a commissar, remove one model from the unit and re-roll the dice. Note that there is no choice in the matter. The second result stands as normal - the commissar may only make a single re-roll for each unit affected. This rule does not apply to units other than infantry, and does not apply to infantry units already reduced to one or two models, or consisting of one or two models to start with.
Massed Batteries - When rolling to determine the 'Fire for effect!' radius (D6+6in) from the aiming point of an artillery barrage, instead of rolling one die roll two dice and take the highest score.

Lack of Radios - When you give the Command Vehicle special rule to a vehicle that does not have it in its entry for the purposes of choosing a command vehicle for an Armoured Platoon, you can give it the rule for free instead of paying the normal +10pts. keywords.name: Low Angle Fire
keywords.definition: All Japanese light mortars have a minimum range of 6in and not the usual 12in. All knee mortars in a unit must be used against the same target. This target may be a different unit to the other non-mortar armed models in the firing unit, int he same way as one-shot weapons; Armies of Imperial Japan, 3rd Edition: Pg. 25

keywords.name: Giretsu
keywords.definition: When outflanking, this unit ignores the -1 modifier to the order test for coming onto the table, and in addition, they remain Fanatics even when reduced to a single man; Armies of Imperial Japan, 3rd Edition: Pg. 25

keywords.name: Ampulomet
keywords.definition: If an Ampulomet hits an armored vehicle and fails to penetrate its armor, roll a die. On the score of a 6 the vehicle is 'on fire' as described for a damage result of 3 on the Damage Results on Armored Vehicles Table; Bolt Action, 3rd Edition: Pg. 257

keywords.name: Remote Operated Mine
keywords.definition: The Goliath model itself is just a marker, and it is treated as a one-shot weapon with a range of 18in. Goliaths can only target stationary vehicles (i.e. any vehicle that has not received an order dice showing a Run or Advance order) or a unit inside a building. Goliaths are fired as normal, except that instead of rolling to hit, roll on the following chart. Note that if a Recce vehicle reacts to the Goliath attack by moving, the mine automatically scores a result of 1-4. Dice 1-4: The Goliath breaks down, or is damaged and prematurely detonated by enemy fire. The Goliath model is removed and has no effect. Dice 5-6: The Goliath reaches the target and is detonated. If the target is a vehicle, it suffers a hit with a PEN of +7 (no PEN modifiers apply). If the target is a unit inside a building, the unit is hit by the equivalent of a heavy howitzer - if this explosion scores 10 or more hits, it brings down the entire building, killing everyone inside; Armies of Germany, 3rd Edition: Pg. 48

keywords.name: Sturmpistole
keywords.definition: This weapon is treated like a panzerfaust, except that it only has a range of 6in and a Pen value of +3. It can, however, be fired normally once a turn and not just once per game; Bolt Action, 3rd Edition: Pg. 204

keywords.name: Demolition Charge
keywords.definition: A unit may place a demolition charge once per game by taking a Fire order. Place a marker (on a 25mm round base) in base contact with a single man in the firing unit. ONce placed, if the placing unit is assaulted by an enemy, or destroyed in any way, the marker is removed. To trigger the charge, the unit must make a Run order in a subsequent turn and move at least 3in away (this cannot be used to assault an enemy unit). After the Run move is complete, the demolition charge immediately explodes, with the 3in template centered on the marker. If the marker is placed in contact with a building, when it explodes treat this as a direct hit by a 3in HE weapon against the building (and any unit inside) instead of using the template. If the marker is placed in contact with a vehicle, and it expodes before the vehicle moves away, treat this as a direct hit by a 3in HE weapon against the vehicle instead of using the template; Armies of Germany, 3rd Edition: Pg. 24

keywords.name: Independent Operative
keywords.definition: 5th Columnists cannot be taken as a compulsory unit for any platoon. They cannot use any national special rules, cannot claim any leadership or activation bonuses from officers and cannot be activated by the first die drawn out of the bag each turn; Armies of Germany, 3rd Edition: Pg. 44

keywords.name: Slow (Towing)
keywords.definition: This unit receives the Slow special rule when towing; Armies of Germany, 3rd Edition: Pg. 44

keywords.name: Tracked Bike
keywords.definition: This unit moves as a half-track; Bolt Action, 3rd Edition: Pg. 218

keywords.name: Squeeze-Bore
keywords.definition: At ranges of up to 12in, its base armor penetration is increased by 2 to a total of +6, and over half-range armor penetration is reduced by 2 to a total of +2; Bolt Action, 3rd Edition: Pg. ???

keywords.name: Super-Heavy Mortar
keywords.definition: Treat this weapon as a heavy howitzer, except that it may only fire indirectly, and has a range of 12-72in; Armies of the Soviet Union, 3rd Edition: Pg. 54

keywords.name: Integrated Tractor
keywords.definition: This allows the gun to be moved by its crew as if it were a medium howitzer; Armies of the Soviet Union, 3rd Edition: Pg. 54

keywords.definition: Can also fire as a low velocity light anti-tank gun - 48in range, 1 shot, PEN+3; Armies of Imperial Japan, 3rd Edition: Pg. 45

keywords.name: Remote Controlled
keywords.definition: It is assumed the vehicle operator is just outside the gaming area, operating the vehicle by remote. After giving a successful order to the Borgward B-IV, and before it moves, roll a die. On a roll of 1 the radio transmitter has lost contact with the vehicle: instead of executing the order, it simply goes Down where it is. On a roll of 2 the transmitter is malfunctioning: the Borgward B-IV makes a reverse move directly backwards instead of the order envisioned by the player controlling the vehicle. On any other roll (3-6) the Borgward V-IV acts normally. If a roll ever needs to be taken on another chart that affects the Borgward V-IV's movement, both rolls need to be taken; Armies of Germany, 3rd Edition: Pg. 73

keywords.name: Heavy Charge
keywords.definition: In order to use the charge, the Borgward must be successfully ordered to Advance. Before moving, place a 4in template in contact with the center of the front hull of the vehicle, then execute a reverse move straight back. After this, any model hit by the template counts as hit by a heavy howitzer, except that the PEN is +5 and that units in building (and the buildings themselves) suffer 4D6 hits instead; Armies of Germany, 3rd Edition: Pg. 73

keywords.name: Reinforced Front Armor
keywords.definition: Against all shots hitting the front of the vehicle it counts its damage value as 1 higher than the damage value given in the entry; Bolt Action, 3rd Edition: Pg. 150

keywords.name: Reinforced Rear Armor
keywords.definition: This vehicle treats hits against the rear armor as hits against the side armor (i.e. +1 penetration modifier rather than +2); Bolt Action, 3rd Edition: Pg. 210

keywords.name: 128mm KwK 44
keywords.definition: This gun does not suffer the -1 penetration penalty when shooting at targets over half range. It counts as a full +7 penetration bonus at all ranges; Armies of Germany, 3rd Edition: Pg. 63

keywords.name: Squeeze-Bore EW 141
keywords.definition: At ranges of up to 18in, its base armor penetration is increased by 1 to a total of +3; Armies of Germany, 3rd Edition: Pg. 57

keywords.name: Experimental EW 141
keywords.definition: When rolling to hit, if a double 1 is rolled, reduce the gun's Shots value to 1 for the rest of the game; Armies of Germany, 3rd Edition: Pg. 57

keywords.name: Schürzen
keywords.definition: If a German tank has Schürzen, then anti-tank rifles and shaped charges never get the +1 penetration bonus for hitting the vehicle in the side; Bolt Action, 3rd Edition: Pg. 210

keywords.name: Götterdämmrung
keywords.definition: Roll a die every time the vehicle completes a move: 1 - The vehicle is immobilized for the rest of the game. 2 - The vehicle may make one more move after this one, then is immobilized. 3+ - Continue as normal, rolling again after the next move; Armies of Germany, 3rd Edition: Pg. 210

keywords.name: Mobile Fortress
keywords.definition: There is no penetration modifier for hitting a Maus from the side or top, and the penetration modifier for hitting a Maus in its rear arc is reduced to +1; Armies of Germany, 3rd Edition: Pg. 210

keywords.name: Dual Direction Steering
keywords.definition: A recce vehicle may move at its full Run speed when going backwards; Bolt Action, 3rd Edition: Pg. 150

keywords.name: Dual Mode Suspension
keywords.definition: This vehicle counts as either tracked or wheeled each turn - declare just before moving; Armies of Germany, 3rd Edition: Pg. 85

keywords.name: Jettison Fuel Trailer
keywords.definition: The normal bonus for trying to damage flamethrowing vehicles does not apply; Bolt Action, 3rd Edition: Pg. 242

keywords.name: Flotation Screen
keywords.definition: DD Shermans moving through deep water through any part of their move may not fire any of their weapons. DD Shermans starting their turn in shallow water may lower their flotation screens and fire their weapons normally; Armies of the United States, 3rd Edition: Pg. 64

keywords.name: Bulldozer Blades
keywords.definition: Tanks with dozer blades can clear an adjacent obstacle by receiving a Down order. The gap in the obstacle becomes rough ground. A Down order may also be used to fill in an anti-tank ditch. Tanks equipped with Bulldozer Blades can assautl buildings even though they are not heavy tanks. When rolling against a building during an assault, treat this vehicle as a super-heavy tank (Damage Value and Front Armor 11); Armies of the United States, 3rd Edition: Pg. 65

keywords.name: Winter Vehicle
keywords.definition: The Aerosan can only travel over snow or flat ice - when doing so it is treated as a wheeled vehicle moving over open ground, and therefore cannot pass through obstacles. All passengers must be equipped with skis; Armies of the Soviet Union, 3rd Edition: Pg. 86

keywords.name: Light HE
keywords.definition: Instead of an HE 3in, the super heavy anti-tank gun has HE 1in; Armies of Great Britain, 3rd Edition: Pg. 58

keywords.name: Deflate Those Tyres
keywords.definition: SAS Jeeps may Advance through areas of difficult ground classified as sandy, rocky, or anything similar; Armies of Great Britain, 3rd Edition: Pg. 85

keywords.name: Littlejohn Adapter
keywords.definition: This weapon has PEN+5, but cannot fire HE. If you roll a 1 (before modification) when you are rolling To Hit, then it breaks and the gun cannot be used for the rest of the game; Armies of Great Britain, 3rd Edition: Pg. 24

keywords.name: Extra Selection - British Motorcycles
keywords.definition: You may take up to three Motorcyle and Sidecars as one selection in each Armored Platoon. A maximum of one light mortar and one anti-tank rifle may be taken in each platoon; Armies of Great Britain, 3rd Edition: Pg. 80

keywords.name: No Optics
keywords.definition: The main gun suffers an additional -1 to hit modifier; Armies of the Soviet Union, 3rd Edition: Pg. 68

keywords.name: Hastily Repaired
keywords.definition: Whenever this vehicle would suffer Superficial Damage, it instead suffers Full Damage; Armies of the Soviet Union, 3rd Edition: Pg. 68

keywords.name: Factory Worker Crew
keywords.definition: This unit must pass an order test to perform any action, even if it has no pin markers; Armies of the Soviet Union, 3rd Edition: Pg. 68

keywords.name: Big Shell
keywords.definition: Because of the sheer size and explosive power of its shell, the howitzer has PEN+5; Bolt Action, 3rd Edition: Pg. 264

keywords.name: Just a Cart
keywords.definition: Tachanka move as wheeled vehicles. In addition, to represent the vulnerability of the horses, it has been given an unusually low Damage Value, and every time it suffers one or more pin markers as a result of an enemy attack, it automatically suffers one additional pin marker; Armies of the Soviet Union, 3rd Edition: Pg. 77

keywords.name: Ancillary
keywords.definition: May not be given the Command Vehicle special rule for the purposes of creating an Armored Platoon; Armies of the Soviet Union, 3rd Edition: Pg. 77

keywords.name: Battle Flag
keywords.definition: Any infantry or artillery unit within 12in and line of sight to a Battle Flag adds +1 to its morale value. Only one Battle Flag may be included in a force. In addition, if you roll a 1 on the Air Strike table, the enemy cannot target a unit that is within 12in of a flag. A Battle Flag cannot be given to a unit's leader (e.g. NCOs, officers, etc.), or to a model with a Signaling Bugle; Armies of Imperial Japan, 3rd Edition: Pg. 25

keywords.name: Signaling Bugle
keywords.definition: All Inexperienced enemy infantry or artillery units within 36in of a Signaling Bugle suffer from a -1 modifier to their morale value, as long as they have no line of sight to the model carrying the Bugle. Only one Signaling Bugle may be included in a force. A Signaling Bugle cannot be given to a unit's leader (e.g. NCOs, officers, etc.), or to a model with a Battle Flag; Armies of Imperial Japan, 3rd Edition: Pg. 25

keywords.name: Radio
keywords.definition: This unit cannot choose to get the Command Vehicle special rule for free with the Lack of Radios special rule; Armies of Imperial Japan, 3rd Edition: Pg. 55

keywords.name: Mine Rake
keywords.definition: Clear minefields on a roll of 4 or more despite only having a damage value of 7+; Armies of Imperial Japan, 3rd Edition: Pg. 61

keywords.name: Bridging
keywords.definition: Whenever you give a Down order to this unit, you may mark it as having its ramps extended. While ramps are extended the vehicle cannot move, but other vehicles may drive over it and 3in in front and behind it, treating the area as open ground, though vehicles may not use Run orders to cross; Armies of Imperial Japan, 3rd Edition: Pg. 61

keywords.name: Railroad Wheels
keywords.definition: This vehicle treats any railroads on the battlefield as roads; Armies of Imperial Japan, 3rd Edition: Pg. 62

keywords.name: Master of the Hunt
keywords.definition: The Sissi are allowed to make an Advance move and if they do not shoot any weapons then the Sissi can turn their dice to an Ambush order; Bolt Action, April 2025 Get-You-By Finland PDF

keywords.name: Field Medics
keywords.definition: Kaukopartio units always act as though a medic was within 6in of the unit; Bolt Action, April 2025 Get-You-By Finland PDF

keywords.name: Deep Strike Mission
keywords.definition: When a Kaukopartio unit that is outflanking becomes available, it may enter the battle from anywhere along either the right/left table edge (depending on the chosen side) or any point along the enemy's own table edge; Bolt Action, April 2025 Get-You-By Finland PDF

keywords.name: Improved Ballistics
keywords.definition: Against targets within half of its range, adds +1 to its penetration value; Armies of the Soviet Union, 3rd Edition: Pg. 58

keywords.name: Slow... Pitifully Slow
keywords.definition: Any vehicle with the Slow special rule has a basic move rate of 6in when Advancing and at a Run. It can still be given a Run order (thereby avoiding the 'One Man Turret' rule) but moves at its basic speed only; Bolt Action, April 2025 Get-You-By Belgium PDF

keywords.name: Mobile Reserve
keywords.definition: Cavalry with this special rule may not move into contact with an enemy unit while mounted and do not suffer the -1 to their leadership roll to arrive from reserve; Bolt Action, February 2026 Get-You-By Bulgaria PDF

keywords.name: Hybrid Gun
keywords.definition: When ordering the gun to Advance, as well as repositioning it, the barrel of the gun can be changed, turning it from a light anti-tank gun into a light howitzer (or vice versa). Declare what barrel the gun starts the game with when you deploy it; Bolt Action, February 2026 Get-You-By Bulgaria PDF

keywords.name: Two-Rocket Salvo
keywords.definition: This weapon has two munition types. Declare which profile you are using before firing. You must load two rockets of the same type, so the next shot taken on the subsequent turn will need to use the same profile. Then, when both rockets have been fired, you can start the process again; Bolt Action, February 2026 Get-You-By Hungary PDF

keywords.name: Small Carriage
keywords.definition: This weapon is too small to tow behind a vehicle. The crew and weapon are instead counted as infantry being transported, taking up 6 transport slots inside a vehicle. The crew may move the weapon up to 6in when given a Run order, even over rough ground; Bolt Action, February 2026 Get-You-By Hungary PDF

keywords.name: One, Not Both!
keywords.definition: This crew may either shoot the main gun or the crew-carried machine gun - but not both; Bolt Action, February 2026 Get-You-By Hungary PDF

keywords.name: Non Testati
keywords.definition: Immediately before the opponent rolls to hit when shooting or for casualties in close combat versus a Camicie Nere section, the controlling player rolls a D6. On a result of 1-2, the section loses its will to fight and gains the Shirkers special rule. On a 3-4, the section remains the same. On a 5-6, the section gains the Fanatics special rule. Apply the ability before resolving the shooting or close combat. The result rolled then applies for the rest of the game; Bolt Action, April 2025 Get-You-By Italy PDF

keywords.name: Too Many Turrets!
keywords.definition: It is always necessary to make an order test when issuing an Advance order, even if the vehicle is not pinned; Bolt Action, April 2025 Get-You-By Italy PDF

keywords.name: Stubborn As A Mule
keywords.definition: When taking an order test and any doubles are rolled, the mules become stubborn and refuse to cooperate, even if the order test was passed. Place the order die to Down and add 1 pin marker to the team. This rule does not apply if a Fubar is rolled; Bolt Action, April 2025 Get-You-By Italy PDF

keywords.name: Gun Assembly
keywords.definition: To simulate the fact that the gun was actually transported disassembled, when the gun is unlimbered the artillery unit receives a pin marker. When the gun is limbered, the mule team (and consequently the 'transported' artillery unit) receives a pin marker; Bolt Action, April 2025 Get-You-By Italy PDF

keywords.name: Poor Maintenance
keywords.definition: When rolling to determine whether the flamethrower runs out of fuel, you suffer a -1 modifier to the roll; Bolt Action, February 2026 Get-You-By Partisans PDF

keywords.name: Lances
keywords.definition: Units equipped with lances gain one additional attack in close quarters against infantry and artillery units, but may not fire their carbines while mounted. Lances are discarded if the unit dismounts; Bolt Action, April 2025 Get-You-By Poland PDF

keywords.name: Too Many Jobs!
keywords.definition: It is always necessary to make an order test when issuing an Advance order, even if the vehicle is not pinned. In addition, the vehicle may fire either the main gun or the turret-mounted medium machine gun in the same turn, but not both; Bolt Action, April 2025 Get-You-By Italy PDF

keywords.name: Severely Outdated
keywords.definition: Antiquated Dutch artillery is not precise enough to fire accurate artillery bombardments, and thus always needs a 6 to hit their target unit when firing indirect fire, even if firing on the same unit in subsequent turns; Bolt Action, April 2025 Get-You-By Italy PDF

keywords.name: Indomitable Spirit
keywords.definition: Ignore all Negative Modifiers when taking Order Tests; Bolt Action, 3rd Edition, Warlord website

keywords.name: Experimental
keywords.definition: Requires an additional Order Test; Bolt Action, 3rd Edition: Pg. ---

keywords.name: 360° Arc
keywords.definition: Can Fire all around; Bolt Action, 3rd Edition: Pg. 135

keywords.name: Right Arc
keywords.definition: Can Fire Right Arc; Bolt Action, 3rd Edition: Pg. 135

keywords.name: Left Arc
keywords.definition: Can Fire Left Arc; Bolt Action, 3rd Edition: Pg. 135

keywords.name: Front Arc
keywords.definition: Can Fire Forward; Bolt Action, 3rd Edition: Pg. 135

keywords.name: Rear Arc
keywords.definition: Can Fire Backward; Bolt Action, 3rd Edition: Pg. 135

keywords.name: Pintle
keywords.definition: Flak; When fired against a Ground Target, makes the unit Open Topped until end of Turn; Bolt Action, 3rd Edition: Pg. 136

keywords.name: Improved HE
keywords.definition: Increase HE Value by 1 (I.E. From HE 1in to HE 2in); Bolt Action, 3rd Edition: Pg. ---

keywords.name: Coaxial
keywords.definition: Must choose between firing the Main Gun or Coaxial Weapon; Bolt Action, 3rd Edition: Pg. 135

keywords.name: Airborne Carriage
keywords.definition: When the Unit is taken as Airborne, this weapon counts as Light for Towing Purposes; Bolt Action, 3rd Edition: Pg. ---

keywords.name: Damage Value: 6+
keywords.definition: Destroyed on a Damage Roll of 6+ from all weapons; Bolt Action, 3rd Edition: Pg. 138

keywords.name: Damage Value: 7+
keywords.definition: Superficial damage on a Damage Roll of 7+, full damage on a Damage roll of 8+ (roll twice and take the higher on a Damage roll of 10+); Bolt Action, 3rd Edition: Pg. 138

keywords.name: Damage Value: 8+
keywords.definition: Superficial damage on a Damage Roll of 8+, full damage on a Damage roll of 9+ (roll twice and take the higher on a Damage roll of 11+); Bolt Action, 3rd Edition: Pg. 138

keywords.name: Damage Value: 9+
keywords.definition: Superficial damage on a Damage Roll of 9+, full damage on a Damage roll of 10+ (roll twice and take the higher on a Damage roll of 12+); Bolt Action, 3rd Edition: Pg. 138

keywords.name: Damage Value: 10+
keywords.definition: Superficial damage on a Damage Roll of 10+, full damage on a Damage roll of 11+ (roll twice and take the higher on a Damage roll of 13+); Bolt Action, 3rd Edition: Pg. 138

keywords.name: Damage Value: 11+
keywords.definition: Superficial damage on a Damage Roll of 11+, full damage on a Damage roll of 12+ (roll twice and take the higher on a Damage roll of 14+); Bolt Action, 3rd Edition: Pg. 138

keywords.name: Cumbersome
keywords.definition: This weapon counts as a heavy gun for the purposes of movement. It also counts as a vehicle for number of shots (reflected in the profile); Bolt Action, 3rd Edition: Pg. ---

keywords.name: Immobile
keywords.definition: Once deployed, this unit cannot be moved. In scenarios that do not allow units to start on the table, place this unit within 6in of your table edge as soon as you know which side of the table is yours; Armies of Imperial Japan, 3rd Edition: Pg. 47

keywords.name: Dug In
keywords.definition: This vehicle starts the game having already suffered an Immobilised result. In scenarios that do not allow units to start on the table, place this unit within 6in of your table edge as soon as you know which side of the table is yours; Armies of Imperial Japan, 3rd Edition: Pg. 54

keywords.name: Intelligence Training
keywords.definition: Once per game, at the beginning of any turn (as long as the Intelligence Officer is on the table), the Officer may act on intelligence gathered about the enemy force before the first die is drawn from the dice bag. Roll a D6, a Veteran Officer receives a +1 modifier on the roll, an Inexperienced one receives a -1 modifier. On a 4+, the player using this ability may choose a die from the bag for the first activation. If both players are doing this on the same turn and both succeed in this roll, the results cancel out and the dice is randomly drawn, as normal. Only one Officer in the entire force may have Intelligence Training; Armies of Germany, 3rd Edition: Pg. 26

keywords.name: Selection (Heavy Weapons Rifle Team)
keywords.definition: May be taken instead of a Mortar or Machine Gun Team in a Heavy Weapons Platoon; Bolt Action, 3rd Edition: Pg. ---

keywords.name: Engineering Selection
keywords.definition: This unit may be taken in an Engineering Platoon instead of one of its non-mandatory Engineer squads; Armies of Imperial Japan, 3rd Edition: Pg. 64

keywords.name: Gun Shield
keywords.definition: The crew counts as in soft cover from small arms hits that come from models within the front arc of the gun. Note that hits from heavy weapons, close quarters ttacks, and any attacks that ignore cover saves also ignore the Gun Shield rule; Bolt Action, 3rd Edition: Pg. 126

keywords.name: HE 1in
keywords.definition: Use 1in Template to determine hits. Pen +1 when HE is used. D2 pins (D3 if in building). Infantry and artillery can go Down to halve the hits taken; Bolt Action, 3rd Edition: Pg. 97

keywords.name: HE 2in
keywords.definition: Use 2in Template to determine hits. Pen +2 when HE is used. D2 pins (D6 if in building). Infantry and artillery can go Down to halve the hits taken; Bolt Action, 3rd Edition: Pg. 97

keywords.name: HE 3in
keywords.definition: Use 3in Template to determine hits. Pen +3 when HE is used. D3 pins (2D6 if in building). Infantry and artillery can go Down to halve the hits taken. 10+ hits on a building collapses the building and kills everyone inside; Bolt Action, 3rd Edition: Pg. 97

keywords.name: HE 4in
keywords.definition: Use 4in Template to determine hits. Pen +4 when HE is used. D3 pins (3D6 if in building). Infantry and artillery can go Down to halve the hits taken. 10+ hits on a building collapses the building and kills everyone inside; Bolt Action, 3rd Edition: Pg. 97

keywords.name: HE Special
keywords.definition: Use 4in Template to determine hits. Pen +1 when HE is used. D6 pins (2D6 if in building). Infantry and artillery can go Down to halve the hits taken. 10+ hits on a building collapses the building and kills everyone inside. Whenever this weapon is fired, the crew receive 1 pin to represent the complicated loading procedure; Armies of Imperial Japan, 3rd Edition: Pg. 47

keywords.name: Liason Officer
keywords.definition: Liaison Officers count as Forward Air Observers; Bolt Action, February 2026 Get-You-By Partisan PDF

keywords.name: Ambush Tactics
keywords.definition: When deployed on the table, these units may start the game on Ambush; Armies of Great Britain, 3rd Edition: Pg. 23, Armies of Imperial Japan, 3rd Edition: Pg. 24

keywords.name: Anti-Tank Gun
keywords.definition: AT Guns when using a Fire Order (incl. Ambush) have +1 to Hit when targetting Vehicles; Bolt Action, 3rd Edition: Pg. 96

keywords.name: Wheeled
keywords.definition: Advance: 12in; Run: 24in; Doubled on Roads; Bolt Action, 3rd Edition: Pg. 133

keywords.name: Half-Track
keywords.definition: Advance: 9in; Run: 18in; Doubled on Roads; Bolt Action, 3rd Edition: Pg. 133

keywords.name: Assault
keywords.definition: This weapon suffers no penalty 'to hit' when moving and shooting. In addition, infantry models armed with an assault weapon count as having the Tough Fighters special rule; Bolt Action, 3rd Edition: Pg. 96

keywords.name: Behind Enemy Lines
keywords.definition: When Outflanking as described on page 172, unit ignores the -1 modifier to the Order Test for coming onto the table; Bolt Action, 3rd Edition: Pg. ---

keywords.name: Fixed
keywords.definition: When ordered to Fire, fixed weapons can only target an enemy unit that lies at least partially within their front arc (i.e. within an angle of 45 degrees to either side of their barrel). Targets outside of this arc cannot be shot at with a Fire order. When ordered to Advance, fixed weapons do not move from their position, but can instead be rotated on the spot to face any direction, and can then fire suffering the normal -1 to hit for 'fire on the move'. When ordered to Run, fixed weapons that are carried and crewed by infantry teams move the normal 12in over open ground or 6in over rough ground, obstacles, etc. Fixed weapon units can never assault other units. If assaulted by an enemy, the gun itself is ignored and the crew models are assaulted as normal. Heavy and super-heavy anti-tank guns and heavy howitzers, as well as any lighter gun whose crew is reduced to a single man, cannot be moved by their crew with a Run order (though they may be rotated by way of an Advance order, as normal for fixed weapons). They can only be moved by means of a tow. NOTE: 'platform-mounted', 'rotating platform', or 'turntable' guns can rotate for free (no -1 movement penalty); Bolt Action, 3rd Edition: Pg. 96, 123, 125

keywords.name: Flak
keywords.definition: Can attack aircraft during an Airstrike; Bolt Action, 3rd Edition: Pg. 117

keywords.name: Flamethrower
keywords.definition: Hits from flamethrowers allow no cover saves. When shooting with a flamethrower, roll a single die to hit as normal, but if you score a hit, it is turned into D6 hits (D6+1 for vehicle-mounted flamethrowers). As no saves are allowed, simply roll for damage in the usual manner. Flamethrowers always hit the top armor of vehicles. Also, they do not suffer the -1 PEN penalty when firing at long range against armored vehicles, nor the +1 PEN for firing at point-blank range. Causes D3+1 pins to target, 1 pin to firing unit. A unit hit by a flamethrower must check its morale regardless of casualties. After shooting roll a D6 (for each flamethrower fired). On a result of 1 or 2, the flamethrower has run out of fuel. Infantry must replace the model with an unarmed model, else remove the model instead (no morale check caused). Vehicles suffer no further effects. When rolling for the Vehicle Damage Results table against a vehicle equipped with flamethrowers, add an extra +1 to the roll; Bolt Action, 3rd Edition: Pg. 97

keywords.name: Multiple Flamethrowers
keywords.definition: The vehicle can only use one flamethrower per turn; Bolt Action, 3rd Edition: Pg. 209

keywords.name: Small Vehicle Flamethrowers
keywords.definition: Small vehicle flamethrowers cause D6 rather than D6+1 hits; Bolt Action, 3rd Edition: Pg. 245

keywords.name: Howitzer
keywords.definition: Can either shoot directly at a target drawing its line of fire 'over open sights' in the normal way, or it can shoot indirect fire. When using indirect fire, a howitzer has a minimum range; when firing over open sights it has no minimum range; Bolt Action, 3rd Edition: Pg. 100

keywords.name: Indirect Fire
keywords.definition: Cannot hit targets within their minimum range, measured from the center of the weapon itself. Units hit by indirect fire receive no cover saves of any kind. However, if the target unit is or goes Down when shot at with indirect fire, the number of hits suffered is still halved. When fired against vehicles, hits from indirect fire weapons always strike the top armor, counting the +1 penetration modifier ot damage regardless of the actual position of the firer. If an open-topped armored vehicle is hit by indirect fire add the +1 penetration modifier to the roll to damage, and also add +1 to the die roll on the Armored Vehicle Damage Results Tables. Cannot fire indirect fire weapons from Ambush. Indirect fire weapons can fire smoke; Bolt Action, 3rd Edition: Pg. 101, 128

keywords.name: Multiple Launcher
keywords.definition: Counts as a heavy mortar, but its chance of hitting never gets any better than a 6 (no ranging in). All units within 6in of the target and not entirely within the weapon's minimum range can be hit. If a friendly unit is within 6in, you cannot fire and the shot is wasted. The unit firing also receives 1 pin marker. When towed, multiple launchers count as light howitzers; Bolt Action, 3rd Edition: Pg. 102

keywords.name: Heavy Rocket Launcher
keywords.definition: Still counts as a heavy mortar, but fires HE 4in rockets. To represent the fact that it is so slow to reload, after it has fired, it must then be given a successful Rally order before it can be ordered to Fire again; Armies of the Soviet Union, 3rd Edition: Pg. 54

keywords.name: One Shot
keywords.definition: Can be fired once per game. One shot Weapons can Split Fire; Bolt Action, 3rd Edition: Pg. 97

keywords.name: Shaped Charge
keywords.definition: No -1 Pen for Long Range. No +1 Pen for Point-Blank; Bolt Action, 3rd Edition: Pg. 103

keywords.name: Smoke Shells
keywords.definition: Can fire Smoke Screen. See Full Rules; Bolt Action, 3rd Edition: Pg. 128

keywords.name: Team Weapon
keywords.definition: A Team Weapon shoots at full effectiveness so long as there are at least two team members to serve it. If only one man remains to serve a team weapon, then the weapon suffers a -1 'to hit' penalty. For squad-based team weapons, loaders must remain within 1in or the weapon suffers the -1 to-hit penalty; Bolt Action, 3rd Edition: Pg. 103

keywords.name: Open Topped
keywords.definition: Pinned by hits from small arms in the same way as soft-skins and infantry. If assaulted by infantry, open-topped armored vehicles are destroyed automatically if the vehicle is damaged, in the same way as soft-skins. If hit against top armor then add an additional +1 to the damage result roll. Note that all hits upon the upper surface of armored vehicles count +1 penetration regardless of whether the target is open or not - so open-topped armored vehicles suffer a double penalty: +1 penetration and +1 damage result; Bolt Action, 3rd Edition: Pg. 149

keywords.name: Bicycles
keywords.definition: When moving on roads, they double their Run move to 24in (cannot be used to Assault). THe first time they receive any order other than Run, or if they receive a Pin marker, they dismount and abandon their bicycles for the rest of the game; Bolt Action, 3rd Edition: Pg. 119

keywords.name: Cavalry
keywords.definition: Can dismount and fight on foot as infantry, from which point none of these rules apply - need to replace mounted figures with non-mounted figures. When cavalry, moves 9in at an Advance and 18in at Run. Cannot enter buildings or board transport vehicles unless they have dismounted. Cannot gain advantages of Down, and their cover saves are always reduced by 1. Can escape as a Recce vehicle (at normal speed, not double speed). Can dismount as part of an Advance move - cannot remount. Can only fire pistol or carbine (treated as pistol) when mounted. While mounted, cavalry have the Tough Fighters special rule. Can regroup up to 2D6in after combat.; Bolt Action, 3rd Edition: Pg. 119

keywords.name: Engineers
keywords.definition: Negates Defenders Bonus when assulting into fortifications/defences; Bolt Action, 3rd Edition: Pg. 120

keywords.name: Fanatics
keywords.definition: If forced to take a morale check, they ignore negative modifiers from pin markers, so long as the unit includes at least two men. Remember that order tests are not morale checks. Fanatic units with at least two men left are not routed and destroyed when they have a number of pin markers equal to or higher than their morale value. When a fanatics unit is defeated in close quarters fighting, the fight counts as a draw instead and another round is immediately fought. Continue fighting until the fanatics unit wins, is completely wiped out, or is defeated and left with a single model, in which case it is destroyed; Bolt Action, 3rd Edition: Pg. 120

keywords.name: Fieldcraft
keywords.definition: Treats rough ground as open ground instead; Bolt Action, 3rd Edition: Pg. 120

keywords.name: Green
keywords.definition: Green units are Inexperienced and have a morale rating of 8. The first time the unit suffers a casualty, roll a die (after taking any morael checks caused by the attack). On a roll of a 1 the unit suffers an additional D6 pin markers and goes Down. THere is no further effect. On a 2, 3, 4, or 5 the unit fights on. There is no further effect. On a 6 the unit is immediately up-rated to Regular with a morale value of 9 for the rest of the battle; Bolt Action, 3rd Edition: Pg. 120

keywords.name: Independent
keywords.definition: ----; Bolt Action, 3rd Edition: Pg. ---

keywords.name: Infiltrator
keywords.definition: If the unit takes a cover save while it does not have an Advance or Run order dice on it, it receives an additional +1 to the roll. In addition, the unit might benefit from special deployment rules, as detailed in the scenario being played; Bolt Action, 3rd Edition: Pg. 120

keywords.name: Inspiring Presence
keywords.definition: ----; Bolt Action, 3rd Edition: Pg. ---

keywords.name: Medics
keywords.definition: If the medic's own unit, or any friendly infantry or artiller unit that has a model within 6in of the medic model itself, suffers damage from small arms fire, one die is rolled for each point of damage caused. On a 6, that damage is ignored and does not cause a casualty. Note that a medic cannot be used against damage inflicted by heavy weapons, nor against damage suffered in close quarters combat. Medic units can't fire any weapons (including those of a transport vehicle they are on), nor assault into close quarters. They will fight in close quarters if assaulted. NOte that medic units and their dice are always ignored for the purpose of victory conditions, for both sides (they cannot capture objectives, they are worth nothing when killed, etc.); Bolt Action, 3rd Edition: Pg. 113

keywords.name: Motorcycles
keywords.definition: Moves at 12in at an Advance and 24in at a Run with the same movement rules and restrictions as wheeled vehicles, exept they may make any number of turns as they move. Cannot enter buildings or board transports. Do not benefit from any advantage from going/being Down. Can react by making an escape move in the same way as recce (at normal move, not double speed). Can dismount as part of any Adcane move and fight as infantry, but cannot remount. Motorcycle riders cannot shoot while moving. Cannot assault and if assaulted can make an escape move as for other recce vehicles. If attacked at close quarters, each man fights as infantry. Regroup 2D6in rather than D6in; Bolt Action, 3rd Edition: Pg. 121

keywords.name: Observer
keywords.definition: Can be used as a spotter for Mortars or Howitzers; Bolt Action, 3rd Edition: Pg. 113

keywords.name: Self-Defence
keywords.definition: Unit cannot fire any weapons (including those of a transport vehicle they are on), nor assault into close quarters. They will fight in close quarters if assaulted. Note that unit and their dice are always ignored for the purpose of victory conditions, for both sides (e.g. they cannot capture objectives, they are worth nothing when killed, etc.); Bolt Action, 3rd Edition: Pg. 113

keywords.name: Shirkers
keywords.definition: Pins count double and must always take an order test, even without pins; Bolt Action, 3rd Edition: Pg. 121

keywords.name: Skis
keywords.definition: Troops ignore movement penalties for Snow or Winter Conditions; Bolt Action, 3rd Edition: Pg. ---

keywords.name: Sniper
keywords.definition: If a sniper team includes a second man, the sniper rifle has the Team Weapon special rule. This means that, if the leader is killed, the second man can fire the sniper rifle, with the usual -1 penalty to hit (as well as the -1 penalty to Morale due to the loss of the leader). Unlike other units with the Team Weapon special rule, all members of a sniper team can fire any weapon they are carrying in any turn when the sniper is not using his scope, and in an assault they can use beneficial rules, like those from submachine guns, tough fighters, etc. When a sniper shoots using a Fire or Ambush order, the player can decide if the sniper uses the rifle's scope, in which case the following apply: The rifle changes its range to 12-36in, the shot benefits from an additional +1 modifier to hit, any hits go straight to damage, no cover saves allowed and benefit from a +1 modifier on damage rolls against infantry and artillery units. If the sniper successfully rolls to hit and damage, the firing player can pick the squad leader in the target unit as a casualty. This includes NCOs, leaders of weapon teams and artillery teams, officers, medics, observers, and so forth; Bolt Action, 3rd Edition: Pg. 122

keywords.name: Lone Sniper
keywords.definition: A lone sniper has the Sniper special rule. As he is unaccompanied, he does not have the Team Weapon rule and therefore does not suffer the -1 to hit for not having a spotter; Armies of Imperial Japan, 3rd Edition: Pg. 43

keywords.name: Spotters
keywords.definition: Cannot be placed within coherency of the weapon crew. Either the weapon crew or the spotter can be given an order - but not both. Spotters can never assault or fire any weapon against enemy units. Spotters without an order die next to it count as Down. Spotters have the Infiltrators special rule. Spotters/observers can only spot for a single Indirect Fire weapon per game turn. If the firing unit switches to a different spotter it resets the ranging-in process. Cannot spot for inexperienced indirect fire weapons. When the associated weapon unit is destroyed, the spotter is removed also. Spotters are always ignored for the purpose of victory conditions. If the spotter is destroyed, the weapons team or artillery unit is not affected (other than that it has no spotter). If already ranged in when the spotter is destroyed, the weapon team can continue firing at 2+; Bolt Action, 3rd Edition: Pg. 102

keywords.name: Stubborn
keywords.definition: If forced to take a morale check, they ignore negative morale modifiers from pin markers. Remember that order tests are not morale checks, and are therefore modified as normal; Bolt Action, 3rd Edition: Pg. 122

keywords.name: Tank Hunters
keywords.definition: As a Winner in Close combat with an Armored Vehicle, resolve results on Damage Table. Squad does not suffer from Tanke Fear; Bolt Action, 3rd Edition: Pg. 121

keywords.name: Tough Fighters
keywords.definition: Model rerolls 1st Failed to Damage in Closed Combat; Bolt Action, 3rd Edition: Pg. 122

keywords.name: Tough Fighters (Shin Gunto)
keywords.definition: Model rerolls 1st Failed to Damage in Closed Combat and rolls one additional dice against infantry/artillery if it has 'Tough Fighters' already; Armies of Japan, 3rd Edition, Pg. ??

keywords.name: Winter equipment
keywords.definition: Any infantry unit may take skis for no additional cost. An infantry unit equipped with skis ignore all negative movement effects related to snow or ice in scenarios that introduce them. Any artillery units may be upgraded to mounted guns for no additional cost, but you must remove all gun shields from any gun upgraded in this way. Any unit with this upgrade is not affected by difficult ground like other artillery. Instead, it may move through difficult ground in the same manner as infantry, and ignores all negative movement effects related to snow or ice in scenarios that introduce them; Armies of Germany, 3rd Edition: Pg. 23

keywords.name: Amphibious
keywords.definition: An amphibious vehicle can move directly forward only over otherwise impassable deep water at half speed by means of an Advance action. A vehicle cannot make any other action whilst moving over water - it cannot reverse, cannot turn, and will ignore all rules that otherwise oblige it to reverse or go Down. A vehicle that is immobilized whilst in the water is destroyed along with any occupants. Vehicles can shoot whilst afloat except hull mounted weapons on vehicles equipped with floatation screens; Bolt Action, 3rd Edition: Pg. 149

keywords.name: Armored All Round
keywords.definition: No Pen modifiers when being shot at in the side, rear, or from above; Bolt Action, 3rd Edition: Pg. 149

keywords.name: Command Vehicle
keywords.definition: Adds morale bonus of +1 to itself and friendly vehicles within 12in and may use Snap To; Bolt Action, 3rd Edition: Pg. 113

keywords.name: Fast
keywords.definition: Tracked Vehicles with Fast Advance at 12in and Run at 24in; Bolt Action, 3rd Edition: Pg. 149

keywords.name: High Rate of Fire
keywords.definition: The Type 97 has 2 shots rather than the normal 1 for an anti-tank rifle. Note however, that it also has the Fixed special rule; Armies of Imperial Japan, 3rd Edition: Pg. 40

keywords.name: Medical Vehicle
keywords.definition: When a friendly inf. or arty unit within 6in suffer damage from Small Arms, roll a D6 for each Damage. On a 6, ignore that damage; Bolt Action, 3rd Edition: Pg. 149

keywords.name: One Man Turret
keywords.definition: Must take an order test when issuing an Advance order, even if the vehicle is not pinned. In addition, you can fire either the main gun or any rear-mounted machine gun, but not both in the same turn; Bolt Action, 3rd Edition: Pg. 149

keywords.name: Recce
keywords.definition: Can Reverse at Full Advance Speed. Has access to 'Escape' Reaction; Bolt Action, 3rd Edition: Pg. 150

keywords.name: Frontal Armor
keywords.definition: Frontal Armor Value is +1; Bolt Action, 3rd Edition: Pg. 150

keywords.name: Slow
keywords.definition: Any vehicle with the Slow special rule has a basic move rate of 6in when Advancing and 12in at a Run; Bolt Action, 3rd Edition: Pg. 150

keywords.name: Slow Load
keywords.definition: The vehicle cannot be given an order until at least one other unit on the same side has already been given orders (whether successfully or not). If an army is left with a number of units which all have the Slow Load special rule, when the army receives its first order dice of the turn, put the dice back in the bag and draw again. THe next dice drawn for that army can then be allocated to a model with Slow Load as if another unit had already been ordered; Bolt Action, 3rd Edition: Pg. 151

keywords.name: Rocket Mortar
keywords.definition: The rocket mortar is treated as a heavy howitzer with only half the normal range (for both direct and indirect fire). The devastating blast of the 380mm rocket mortar allows the player to re-roll all dice that failt o score damage from the blast, as well as the dice for the number of pin markers. In addition, it inflicts 4D6 hits (and D6 pins) on targets inside buildings; Bolt Action, 3rd Edition: Pg. 213, February 2025 errata

keywords.name: Stationary Firing Platform
keywords.definition: The vehicle may not fire if given an Advance order; Armies of Germany, 3rd Edition: Pg. 76, June 2025 errata

keywords.name: Turn On The Spot
keywords.definition: Can execute a full speed Run 'reverse' finishing the move facing in the direction of travel; Bolt Action, 3rd Edition: Pg. 151

keywords.name: Turret Rear Arc
keywords.definition: Fires opposite arc of the Main Gun or Coax after the Main or Coax is fired; Bolt Action, 3rd Edition: Pg. 151

keywords.name: Unreliable
keywords.definition: When vehicle suffers at least 1 pin, it suffers 1 additional pin; Bolt Action, 3rd Edition: Pg. 151

keywords.name: Unpredictable
keywords.definition: Any time a Home Defense unit fails an order test, roll a D6: on a 1-2, the unit immediately goes Down, in addition it takes D3 pin markers. On a 3-4, the unit immediately goes Down as normal. On a 5-6, the unit immeidately makes a Run order towards the nearest visible enemy unit. If this move would bring them into contact with that unit, it counts as an assault into close quarters; Armies of Imperial Japan, 3rd Edition: Pg. 24

keywords.name: Versatile - Light Howitzer
keywords.definition: Can also fire as a light howitzer - 48in range, 1 shot, HE 2in OR indirect with 30-60in range, 1 shot, HE 2in; Bolt Action, 3rd Edition: Pg. 259

keywords.name: Versatile - Medium Howitzer
keywords.definition: Can also fire as a medium howitzer - 48in range, 1 shot, HE 3in OR indirect with 30-60in range, 1 shot, HE 3in; Bolt Action, 3rd Edition: Pg. 259

keywords.name: Versatile - Medium AT Gun
keywords.definition: Can also fire as a medium anti-tank gun - 60in range, 1 shot, PEN+5; Bolt Action, 3rd Edition: Pg. 259

keywords.name: Weak Sides
keywords.definition: All shots to the side of the vehicle count as to the rear (i.e. they have a +2 penetration modifier rather than +1); Bolt Action, 3rd Edition: Pg. 151

keywords.name: Iron Discipline
keywords.definition: This unit may remove 2 pin markers rather than the usual one if an Order Test is passed; Bolt Action, 3rd Edition German Army Book: Pg. 23

keywords.name: Mixed Quality
keywords.definition: InEx Only; Roll a D6 on a Failed Order Test, See Full Rules; Bolt Action, 3rd Edition German Army Book: Pg. ---

keywords.name: Rangers Lead the Way!
keywords.definition: After setup, but before the first turn of the game as a part of beginning of game actions, this unit may make a Run Move; Bolt Action, 3rd Edition German Army Book: Pg. ---

keywords.name: Vickers K
keywords.definition: Counts as a light machine gun but fires one additional shot (i.e. 5 shots for infantry-carried guns, 3 shots for vehicle-mounted guns, 5 shots vs. aircraft); Armies of Great Britain, 3rd Edition: Pg. 24

keywords.name: Who Dares Wins!
keywords.definition: InEx Only; Roll a D6 on a Failed Order Test, See Full Rules; Bolt Action, 3rd Edition German Army Book: Pg. ---

keywords.definition: Ground Attack Aircraft comes in on a 4, 5, or 6. If a Ground Attack Aircraft performs the airstrike, 5 Hits are required to bring it down; Bolt Action, 3rd Edition : Pg. ---

keywords.name: Flying Tank - Experimental
keywords.definition: Ignore the first Exceptional Damage Result of the game against this unit; Bolt Action, 3rd Edition : Pg. ---

keywords.definition: When resolving Fire For Effect!, resolve the D6+6in by rolling 2D6 and picking the highest to use for the D6+6in; Bolt Action, 3rd Edition : Pg. ---
